I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery `DELETE FROM ... WHERE ... IN (SELECT ...)` instead of a direct `DELETE FROM ...`.

### Cause
In `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`, the compiler evaluated whether the deletion query involved a single table by checking `self.query.alias_map`. For querysets without existing filter or join clauses (such as `Model.objects.all()`), `get_initial_alias()` had not yet been called on `self.query`, leaving `alias_map` empty (`{}`). As a result, active table count was 0, causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False` and falling back to a subquery DELETE.

### Fix
Updated `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias` in [`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1414) to invoke `self.query.get_initial_alias()` when `self.query.count_active_tables() == 0`. This populates the primary table alias before checking if `count_active_tables() == 1`, allowing un-filtered querysets to generate direct single-table `DELETE FROM table` SQL statements.
